name: equity-condor-robust-backtest
notes: DRAFT for ADR-0255 (PROPOSED, not approved; nothing here runs until the ADR is approved and the PROPOSED kinds are built). Retrospective research replay, NOT production qualification: one one-lot equity iron condor per ticker-date, chosen by a Wasserstein-ball robust MILP over ALL ordered strike combinations of that date's liquid DTE-31 contracts, held to expiry and settled at the underlying close; early exercise and assignment are ignored and labeled; ENTRY CLOCK (owner, ADR-0255): the fill is the forecast date's own vwap with expiry t+31, labeled 'assumed same-day average fill' because that day's trades overlap the close that feeds the forecast; fills are labeled 'assumed day-average fill' (legs priced at vwap -/+ a per-ticker haircut h, plus a per-contract fee). Single-trade evaluation: no capital interaction, no portfolio claim. 2026 stays closed: both readers are bounded to end before 2026-01-01 (settlements reach 2025-12-29). Nothing is refit and nothing is acquired. Flow: schedule + stock bars + DTE-31 option bars -> checkpoint inference (never a later checkpoint for an earlier date) -> nominal masses at strikes -> monthly prior-only rho calibration -> RobustCondorSelect -> expiry settlement -> dskit.evaluation report. VALUES: every knob below is a param. A value the ADR has not frozen is the string "PLACEHOLDER" (or a TO_REGISTER_* source name) so the run FAILS CLOSED until the owner supplies it; the PROPOSED nodes must refuse a non-numeric knob by name. No foreach: the ticker universe is whatever the registered sources hold, read in one pass, so the document does not list ~400 tickers or fan out ~2,400 nodes. DUPLICATIONS THAT NEED A PIN TEST (ADR-0255 manifest gap): (a) the 2026-01-01 bound appears once per source in stock_bars.sources[*].read_bounds, while option_chain.windows ends (2024-12-31, 2025-11-28) bound that reader, so all three must stay before 2026; (a2) the option stores are named by their own roots (each an onboarding store: option-universe-300 already is; option-universe-100 must be copied out of a worktree to its data home first), while stock_bars.root is the index_options store; (a3) entry.start (2025-02-04) must be at least calibration.end + 31 days + rho_calibration.availability_lag_days, which holds only for a lag of at most 4 days, so a longer lag must refuse; (b) the phase names 'calibration' and 'entry' are declared once in option_chain.windows and named again by rho_calibration.phase/target_phase and select.phase, so a mismatch must refuse; (c) the contract multiplier is declared once (select) and settle reads it from the rows, never restates it. MANIFEST GAPS vs ADR-0255: it names only RobustCondorSelect, 'the replay node' and libs/pyomo.py; this draft also needs ParquetStreamRows, ExactDteBarChain, CheckpointCDFInference, NominalStrikeMasses and HeldOutRhoCalibration (all PROPOSED below), and RobustCondorSelect must override PyomoSolve.role (default 'capital' demands an upstream stat_test, dskit/pipeline/libs/pyomo.py:475). Not yet verifiable here: the vendor's vwap/trade_count/volume column names beyond dskit/onboarding/libs/alpaca.py:1208, and the runtime event-log census (fills->orders->decisions links) of the report.

params.source: PLACEHOLDER: the final checkpoint inventory of the evaluation run (cutoff -> fit identity / fit_root); not yet written

schedule.notes: EXISTS today (dskit/pipeline/kinds_table.py:108, kind 'table-file'). The checkpoint schedule read-in: a JSON object mapping each training cutoff to its fit identity and fit_root, resolved from the evaluation run's final inventory. Every value is a placeholder (zero digest, zero date and a missing file are deliberate), so the run fails closed (sha256 mismatch / missing file) rather than guessing a checkpoint; the inference node additionally refuses any date whose cutoff is not strictly earlier than it. OPEN: a derived table a later run reads should be published through onboarding (localtables, CLAUDE.md 'Data enters through onboarding'); table-file with a repo-relative path is the stand-in until the inventory is onboarded.

stock_bars.notes: PROPOSED by this draft (not in ADR-0255's manifest; tier-2 generic reader in dskit/pipeline/libs/parquet.py): ParquetRows (exists) reads ONE named file per key, so reading ~400 tickers needs a foreach of that many nodes or a relpath map of that many lines; this reads EVERY file of a localblobs stream through payload_files, each hashed against its manifest, and emits {file column -> output field} rows. Closes feed the forecast spot, the as-traded settlement close and the entry calendar. The two sources are the existing onboarded daily-bar stores (configs/source-stock-daily.json, source-stock-daily-300.json); columns are the StockDailyBars schema (index_options/stock_bars.py:36), UNVERIFIED against the stored parquet. read_bounds uses the shared DateBoundedParquet gate so no 2026 row is ever materialized (ParquetRows' read_bounds contract, dskit/pipeline/libs/parquet.py:43). Root is the store, the one absolute path (CLAUDE.md).

as_traded.notes: EXISTS (dskit/pipeline/libs/bar_features.py:457). Option strikes are AS TRADED but the bars' closes are split-adjusted at the data's end, so the spot S_t, the strike-relative weights w_j = (s_{j+1}-s_j)/S_t and the settlement close S_T must all be on the strike basis: close x later split ratios. split_irregular flags a vendor-booked spin-off (non-whole ratio) where this basis is approximate; the tolerance is the one the feature workflow already uses (configs/workflow-features.json:155).

option_chain.notes: PROPOSED by ADR-0255 ('a DTE 31 option-bar reader'; child kind, wraps dskit.onboarding.observations.iter_stream like ObservationStreamRows, dskit/pipeline/libs/observations.py:607). Reads the daily trade-close bars of the stock option stores and keeps ONLY rows whose expiry minus quote_date is exactly dte (calendar days) AND whose quote_date lies in a named window, tagging each row with its window name as 'phase'. Each source names its own onboarding store root with catalog source 'options', stream 'bars': option-universe-300 already is an onboarded store; option-universe-100 must first be copied from the worktree it sits in (pipeline_runs/, forbidden as a data home) to /home/russell/data/stock_options/option-universe-100 and verified with dskit.onboarding verify. 'bars' is the alpaca option-bar stream whose dedupe key is (contract, quote_date) (dskit/onboarding/libs/alpaca.py:726). Calibration window = forecasts 2024-02-06..2024-12-31 (48 DTE-31 dates today), entry window = 2025-02-04..2025-11-28 (43 dates; median 244/298 tickers) - too few dates for strong intervals, stated here and in the report, not hidden. The entry window opens after the last 31-day calibration outcome plus its availability lag (rho_calibration.availability_lag_days). The window ends are the only date limits in the document (besides stock_bars' 2026 bound): the data end is exclusive of 2026. Rows are passed through unfiltered by liquidity - eligibility is select's rule, so the report can sweep it. Output fields: contract, symbol, expiry, right, strike, date, vwap, trade_count, volume, dte, phase. Column names after 'fields' are the registered stream's; vwap/trade_count/volume names are UNVERIFIED against the not-yet-registered stores.

forecasts.notes: PROPOSED by ADR-0255 ('Inference'; child kind). For each (symbol, date) in the chain, pick the schedule row with the LATEST training cutoff strictly earlier than the date, load that nominal (seed 11) checkpoint through dskit.pipeline.libs.predictive_cdf.TorchCDF.load_checkpoint (predictive_cdf.py:2699, which refuses a modified weights hash) using the archived recovery recipe, and emit the standardized-return CDF curve and scale a_t at the date's as-traded spot. FAIL CLOSED: no schedule row before the date, an unresolved schedule value, or an unsupported head -> a skip row (reason names which) and NO trade; a later checkpoint is NEVER applied to an earlier date. 'seed' is the nominal seed named in the ADR, not a training knob (nothing is refit); 'estimator' is the class load_checkpoint is called on and must equal the class in each checkpoint's state.json. 'phases' names which chain phases to infer for (declared in option_chain.windows) so a typo refuses. The horizon is read from the chain rows' dte, not restated here. OPEN item 1 of ADR-0255: day-t vwap overlaps the close that feeds the forecast, so this fill is same-day look-ahead until the forecast origin vs entry clock is verified; the node must record the origin it used. recovery_recipe is a placeholder for the archived recipe's reference (evaluation run inventory).

masses.notes: PROPOSED by ADR-0255 ('Grid and nominal masses'; child kind). Per (symbol, date) it builds the shared grid K = that date's strikes (tails collapse onto the extreme strikes, where a condor's loss is capped) and the nominal masses p_hat: the mass between adjacent strikes is F_hat(s_{k+1}) - F_hat(s_k), placed on the two bounding strikes so the stretch's MEAN is preserved - this keeps every condor's expected loss exact, so no mesh tolerance is needed (replaces the proposal's interior-point rounding; pinned against the exact gridcurve_log_spread_loss integral). 'placement' and 'tails' name strategy objects (a subclass/registry entry per spelling) rather than branches. Output also carries entry spot S_t (as-traded close) and the weights w_j for the W1 constraint. Refuses a non-monotone CDF or masses that do not sum to one (skip row, no trade); the skips port carries the forecasts' skips forward and adds its own.

rho_calibration.notes: PROPOSED by ADR-0255 ('Calibration'; child kind; the rule is close to AdaptiveWassersteinRadius, index_options/cdf_study.py:165, which is a class not a node - wrapping vs reimplementing is a build-time sweep question). rho is the W1 radius as a dimensionless fraction of spot (formulation eq. 2). RULE: the smallest rho in rho_grid whose robust expected loss bounds the AVERAGE realized loss on held-out date blocks (same-date tickers kept together; never scored against a single payoff). UPDATE: monthly and PRIOR-ONLY - the value used for an entry month is fitted only from outcomes settled AND published at least availability_lag_days before the month starts, starting from the calibration phase and growing with settled entries. block_days are CALENDAR days (overlap is a calendar property): primary at least the 31-day horizon, sensitivity longer, each converted to the consecutive entry dates it spans; both reported. The rule is FROZEN before the backtest; nothing here is chosen by test profit. If no rho in the grid passes the bound, the month's rho is null and select declines to trade. FROZEN values (owner may veto at ADR approval): rho_grid and alpha/replicates/seed/min_dates are the existing run-cdf-causal-robust-condor-calibration.json radius_calibration values; the lag is 1 day (a 31-day outcome is the expiry close, published the next session); audit_candidates is the entry-known template 'short put at the nearest listed strike at or below the forecast short_q quantile, short call at or above the 1-short_q quantile, long wings one listed eligible strike beyond' - independent of rho and of outcomes, so the audit is not circular. The smallest passing rho also minimizes the forgone nominal edge among passing values; ablations: nominal (rho=0) versus rho-only. Output ports: rho (month -> rho or null, with the evidence count) and audit.

params.fee_status: PROVISIONAL placeholder until the owner supplies the real figure

select.notes: PROPOSED by ADR-0255 ('Optimizer'; child PyomoSolve subclass in the PyomoSolve doorway, dskit/pipeline/libs/pyomo.py:459, supplying only legs, ordering and payoff; the W1 dual-embedding helper is the generic part in libs/pyomo.py). ONE MILP per ticker-date over ALL x with K_LP<K_SP<K_SC<K_LC drawn from that date's ELIGIBLE contracts - no width, moneyness, OTM or count cap - with the worst-case LP dualized (formulation eq. 3-4, dual variables lambda/alpha/beta/gamma and the no-trade z); a tie goes to NO TRADE (z=0 wins ties). Eligible = both a trade_count and a volume at or above the 'liquidity' thresholds on that date (trade_count >= 5 from the calibration-window distribution - median 3 puts / 4 calls - swept as liquidity_sensitivity). PRICING: sells at vwap - h, buys at vwap + h, plus fee_per_contract_usd per contract; h = haircut.usd_per_share_by_tier[haircut.tier_by_ticker[symbol]] from the tier table (haircut.tiers): ASSUMED values, not measurements - the researched evidence is old (2003-06, 2010) and not by liquidity tier - so the claim rests on the sweep_multiplier grid and the reported breakeven h; tier_by_ticker is computed from the calibration window only; the fee 0.65 is a PROVISIONAL placeholder until the owner supplies it; ENTRY CLOCK (owner, ADR-0255): the fill is the forecast date's own vwap with expiry t+31, labeled 'assumed same-day average fill' because that day's trades overlap the close that feeds the forecast; fills are labeled 'assumed day-average fill'. rho comes per entry month from rho_calibration.rho (null -> no trade). bands.enabled=false: local CDF bands (mu, nu) stay off unless separately supported; if enabled, an empty band set refuses. multiplier is the equity contract multiplier (declared once; settle reads it from the rows). The phase is the option_chain window to trade. Reports per trade the expected breakeven h (the live check) and later the realized backtest breakeven. solver 'appsi_highs' is the pyomo-solve example's (examples/pipeline/pyomo-solve.json); enumeration over all combinations stays the reference on small fixtures only. NOTE: the role must be overridden away from 'capital' by the subclass or the planner demands an upstream stat_test. Outputs: decisions, selections, solves, skips.

settle.notes: PROPOSED by ADR-0255 (the per-ticker daily replay; child kind). For each selected condor: one order and one fill per leg at the selection's vwap -/+ h (fill qty = lots x the row's multiplier, so the book's cash is USD), the fee on each fill, then at expiry a cash flow of -multiplier x the capped intrinsic loss at S_T = the underlying's as-traded close on the settle date, and an outcome carrying the realized USD P&L. S_T is the close of the last bar on or before the expiry, valid only within max_settlement_gap_days calendar days of it and only when a later bar exists (the rule of CondorQuoteBacktest, index_options/nodes.py:1081, MAX_SETTLEMENT_GAP_DAYS = 4; here a param); otherwise the entry is an 'unsettled' skip and is not scored. Early exercise/assignment are IGNORED and 'labels' carries that, and the fill label, into the report's run_start. Single trade per ticker-date: positions do not interact. Outputs: orders, fills, cashflows, outcomes, skips (carried + own).

events.notes: EXISTS (dskit/evaluation/nodes.py:148); the map targets are validated against dskit-eval-v1 at plan time (dskit/evaluation/events.py). Every field name on the right is a column the PROPOSED select/settle nodes must emit (asof_ms is the default instant; known_ms must not exceed it for a decision). Decision per ticker-date: action enter or skip with a reason; one order per leg carries ref_price = the leg's vwap so the report's slippage view shows the haircut h; the fill's tag carries the 'assumed day-average fill' label. No criteria are pre-registered (ADR-0255 sets none: a research replay), so the verdict is expected to be UNJUDGED. The event-log census (every fill linked order -> decision, outcomes strictly after decisions) is checked at run time and could not be verified without the PROPOSED nodes.

report.notes: EXISTS (dskit/evaluation/nodes.py:37). Writes events, summary.md, a self-contained report.html, decisions and trades CSVs under <run dir>/report. A relative out_dir lands inside the run directory; a path beginning with 'pipeline_runs' is refused. The replay is single-trade and retrospective: read the report as evidence about the robust selection rule, not as a portfolio result.
